findings.summary: README.md:86 names the stop, so its edit should not be conditional
findings.evidence: README.md:86 reads "... `budget spent`, `repeated failure` (one item failed twice; it is named), `queue empty` ...". So the condition the plan puts on this edit ("edit line 86 only if it names the stop") is already true. Fix: Make the README.md:86 edit a firm step: take `repeated failure` out of the stop list and add `environment stopped` where it fits, along with the edit at line 126.

findings.summary: docs/spec.toml:1351 will describe a stop that no longer exists
findings.evidence: docs/spec.toml:1351 says "the drain stop reasons in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (a repeated failure stops the drain)". After this change that statement is false. The plan leaves it for a later job as an open question. Fix: Keep the open question, and say in the change description that spec.toml:1351 is now stale, so a stranger reading the spec is not misled. Alternatively ask the user whether this one-phrase edit can go into this change.

findings.summary: Some kept-stop tests are edited, so criterion 2's "pass unchanged" is not literally true
findings.evidence: Criterion 2 says the settings tests pass "unchanged", but the plan rewrites the `Before::RepeatedFailure` seed of `every_landing_path_ends_in_reinstall_for_any_unreadable_config`. It also deletes `assert_ne!(.., Stop::RepeatedFailure)` lines from the disk, budget and other stop tests. Those edits cannot be avoided once the variant is removed. Fix: In the change description, list which kept-stop tests were edited and why (assertions on a removed name deleted, seed moved to Environment). Confirm that no assertion about the kept stop itself was weakened.
findings.location: Demonstration for criterion 2 (matrix seed) and step 5

findings.summary: A check timeout no longer stops the batch; the user should confirm this
findings.evidence: In disk.rs:358-381, StopCause separates LowDisk, CheckTimeout, ProducerAuth, UsageLimit and OtherEnvironment. Today, a check that times out twice on an overloaded machine ends the batch through RepeatedFailure (drain.rs:2426). Under the plan it is passed over and the next item runs, possibly hitting the same timeout. Fix: Add CheckTimeout and OtherEnvironment to the open question about the login stop. That way the user confirms that only an expired login, a usage limit or low disk stops the batch.
findings.location: Decision 2 (CheckTimeout and OtherEnvironment not batch stops)

summary: I read drain.rs, disk.rs, steward.rs, tests/drain.rs and tests/job_plan.rs, and grepped the docs, README and CHANGELOG. The plan fixes the fault where it starts. The only item-level stop is `ItemEnd::Failed => self.set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure, Some(item.job.clone()))` at drain.rs:2426, reached from drain.rs:1841. The plan turns that arm into a `pass_over`, the same call the Paused and Flagged arms make (drain.rs:2460). It also correctly found that the drain has no login stop of its own: grepping drain.rs for login, auth and StopCause found no match, so an expired login stopped the batch only through RepeatedFailure. To keep that stop, the plan reads the last failure's reason with the existing single classifier, `StopCause::of` (disk.rs:388). That uses code that already exists rather than a heuristic, and it keeps ATTEMPTS unchanged. The plan's claims check out against the code. `last_reason` (drain.rs:1413) reads the job line's reason, which is set from `run.reason` (drain.rs:1549). `Report`/`Stop` are only built for output. job_plan.rs:209-214 would stop compiling unless edited. Hestia's `repeated_failures` reads job records, not the drain report (steward.rs:722). The serial drain does not read ahead (tests/drain.rs:1291 shows that b is never read after a's stop). So the criterion 1 test would fail under the old arm and pass under the new one. Athena's own findings, that job_plan.rs and README.md are outside the deliverables, are answered well: job_plan.rs must change for the workspace to build, and README.md would otherwise document a removed stop. Not creating the warm-baseline note is correct per the reading. My remaining findings are minor: README.md:86 does name the stop, so editing it should be a firm step; spec.toml goes stale; the kept-stop tests are not literally unchanged; and passing over CheckTimeout is a behaviour change to confirm with the user. The work fits one producer run.
